title: 🏛️ Exam 2026 technical · reading: a free gardening course ⭐⭐

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, technical — reading, question 1)
A text is written by a person who has joined a free gardening course.

The text is mainly about a person who joined a gardening course to

options.text: win a prize at a flower show

questions.explanation: The writer has always been interested in growing fruit, vegetables and flowers and wanted to learn more about gardening, which means improving her skills. The text mentions no wish to earn money, to change jobs or to win a prize: she already loves her job, so the aim is to learn.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, technical — reading, question 2a, paragraph 1)
The writer of the text introduces the gardening course she joined after work. Is the statement below true or false, going by paragraph 1?

"The writer goes to gardening lessons two times a week."
questions.explanation: The statement is true: a sentence of paragraph 1 says the same in other words. Judge a statement by the words of the paragraph, not by what seems likely.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, technical — reading, question 2a, paragraph 1)
A student says: "The writer goes to gardening lessons two times a week." Which part of paragraph 1 settles whether this statement is true or false?

options.text: I have always been interested in what you can grow
one night a week after work and every Saturday
thinking about learning more about gardening for a long time

questions.explanation: One night a week after work plus every Saturday makes two lessons each week. The other parts say how the writer feels and how long she has been interested, not how often she goes.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, technical — reading, question 2b, paragraph 3)
The writer closes the text by comparing her job with her studies. Decide whether the statement below is true or false, going by paragraph 3.

"The writer finds gardening difficult and boring."
questions.explanation: The statement is false: a sentence of paragraph 3 says the opposite. Judge a statement by the words of the paragraph, not by what seems likely.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, technical — reading, question 2b, paragraph 3)
A student says: "The writer finds gardening difficult and boring." Which part of paragraph 3 settles whether this statement is true or false?

options.text: I love my job but it's a bit depressing
We see a lot of terrible stuff

questions.explanation: The writer calls studying gardening "completely fun": only this part says how she feels about her gardening studies, and it says the opposite of the statement.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, technical — reading, question 3, paragraph 1)
Paragraph 1 says: "When I found out I could do a free technical course, I was really excited."

What does "could" express in this sentence?
questions.explanation: "I could do a free technical course" means that it was possible for her to do it. She does not say she must do it (obligation) or that she plans to do it (intention), and nobody is asking for anything (request).

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, technical — reading, question 4a, paragraph 2)
Paragraph 2 says: "So, we're all just swapping advice."

Which word from paragraph 2 means nearly the same as "exchanging"?
questions.explanation: To swap is to exchange: the students exchange advice with one another. "Advice" is what they swap, "supportive" describes the class and "moved" is a verb of movement.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, technical — reading, question 4b, paragraph 3)
Paragraph 3 says: "We see a lot of terrible stuff and deal with a lot of tough situations."

Which word from paragraph 3 means nearly the same as "difficult"?
questions.explanation: "Tough situations" are difficult situations. "Depressing" and "terrible" describe how bad or sad things are, and "fun" has the opposite feeling.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, technical — reading, question 5a, paragraph 2)
Paragraph 2 says: "Then, we moved on to plant identification, which is fantastic."

What does "which" refer to?

options.text: learning to use garden tools safely

questions.explanation: "Which" stands for the thing that is fantastic: plant identification, the step after the garden tools. Put it back in the sentence: plant identification is fantastic.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, technical — reading, question 5b, paragraph 3)
Paragraph 3 says: "I love my job but it's a bit depressing."

What does "it" refer to?
questions.explanation: Say the sentence with the noun in place of "it": I love my job but my job is a bit depressing. The writer contrasts her work with her gardening studies, so "it" cannot be gardening, her garden or the course.
